scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I need to figure out if the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

The person in question is a student who had to watch their stepbrother for a week. They brought their Nintendo Switch to pass the time during their long train commute. The stepbrother wanted to play on it, and it helped distract him while the student studied. So, the student created a new profile for the stepbrother to prevent him from messing up their saves. 

After the week, when the student returned to school, they got annoyed because they had to switch profiles every time they played a game or went to the eShop. So, they decided to delete the stepbrother's profile. 

Fast forward to Thanksgiving, the student brought the Switch again. The stepbrother tried to play and realized his Zelda save was gone. He got upset, cried a bit, and now is in his room. The dad thinks it was mean to delete the profile, knowing the stepbrother enjoyed playing.

So, the question is: Is it morally acceptable for the student to delete the stepbrother's profile?

Let me break this down. The student created the profile to help the stepbrother, which was kind. But then, after the week, they found it annoying to switch profiles, so they deleted it. The stepbrother was emotionally affected, and the dad disapproved.

I think the key points here are consent, impact on others, and the intention behind the action.

First, when the student created the profile, it was with the stepbrother's permission, right? They wanted to play, so the student set it up. But when the student deleted it, was that okay? The stepbrother didn't consent to having his profile deleted. The student just did it because it was inconvenient for them.

Second, the impact on the stepbrother was significant. He was upset, cried, and now is upset. The dad saw it as mean, which suggests that the action hurt someone's feelings.

Third, the intention was to make things easier for the student, but it came at the cost of the stepbrother's enjoyment and emotional state. The student didn't consider how the stepbrother would feel when they deleted the profile.

So, considering these points, the action seems to be morally unacceptable because it involved deleting something without the other person's consent, caused emotional harm, and was done without considering the impact on the stepbrother.
